# Supported EV chargers, meters, batteries and cars

SpotNav for Home Assistant works with the Home Assistant integrations listed here. The lists are generated from the tables the integration itself uses, so they always match the release.

Each row says how it is known to work:

- **Tested: charging verified**: charging confirmed on real hardware.
- **Set up by users: detected and configured, charging not yet confirmed**: users have added it and SpotNav detected and configured it correctly, but nobody has yet confirmed that charging or current control works.
- **Detected from the integration's source**: SpotNav recognises the integration's entities and follows its documented behaviour, but nobody has confirmed it on real hardware yet.

Using one of these? Tell us whether it works: [Hardware tested](../../../issues/new?template=hardware_report.yml).

Jump to: [inverters and batteries, the overview](#hybrid-inverters-and-home-batteries-overview), [chargers](#supported-ev-chargers), [grid meters](#supported-grid-meters), [house batteries](#supported-house-batteries), [vehicles](#supported-vehicles), [solar forecast](#supported-solar-forecast), [price areas](#supported-price-areas).

## Hybrid inverters and home batteries: overview

Every hybrid inverter and home battery we know of in the Nordics and Europe, and how far SpotNav gets with each. The detailed rows are under [grid meters](#supported-grid-meters) and [house batteries](#supported-house-batteries); what the battery plan needs from each is in [The battery plan](battery-plan.md#what-the-plan-needs).

- **SpotNav reads**: what it finds by itself through the integration. *Untested* means read from the integration's source and not yet confirmed on real hardware. A battery that is not read can still be used by picking its power sensor yourself on the site.
- **SpotNav controls**: *Opt-in, in testing* is [SpotNav's own battery control](home-battery.md#spotnavs-own-battery-control-off-by-default-in-testing), off by default. *Mapped, never run on a device* means SpotNav has the commands for that integration behind the same switch and the same check of the battery, but nobody has run them on a battery yet. *Not mapped* means SpotNav only reads, with what the integration itself could do locally. Without control SpotNav still plans in shadow where it reads the battery's level, and still signals a grid charge to your own planner or automation.
- **Unknown** is where neither SpotNav's tables nor our notes say. Corrections are welcome: [Hardware tested](../../../issues/new?template=hardware_report.yml).

## Supported EV chargers

Add a charger with **Settings, Devices & services, Add integration, SpotNav, A charger, Automatic (recommended)**. SpotNav reads the charger's own integration, suggests the charge control, the current setting, the energy meter and the status sensor, and asks you to confirm. Any other charger that exposes a switch works through **Manual**, which starts and stops the charge and can set a current through a number entity.

### Supported

These integrations can be started and stopped, and most can have their current set. A column that says None means SpotNav does that part without the charger's help: a charger with no current control still follows the plan's start and stop times, and load balancing and solar switch it on and off whole at the current SpotNav learns it draws (see [chargers that can only be switched on and off](site-and-load-balancing.md#chargers-that-can-only-be-switched-on-and-off)).

A charge point with several connectors is added once per connector. The session current limit goes out as a relative charging profile, which Easee over OCPP, KEBA firmware 1.18 and 1.19.0, Autel, and ABB firmware 1.8.37 with the integration's 0.12 versions reject: current control does not work on those. A charging profile left behind can cap the charger; `ocpp.clear_profile` removes it. | Tested: charging verified (Charge Amps HALO) |

### Measurement only

SpotNav cannot start or stop these chargers, so the flow refuses them as a charger with the message that they can only be read. They stay in the catalogue because their energy and current sensors are recognised as measurements.

| Integration | Energy and status | Notes | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tesla Wall Connector (`tesla_wall_connector`) | Lifetime energy | Read only: the car is the actuator. | Detected from the integration's source |

### Controlled by another system

These integrations mean another system owns the charger. The flow shows a warning and suggests nothing, because two controllers on one charger send contradictory commands. Choose the entities yourself only if SpotNav should really take over.

- evcc (`evcc_intg`)
- openWB (`openwb2mqtt`)

These integrations switch or limit a charger by themselves and run beside SpotNav. The flow and the card warn that the charger will be fought over, and still suggest the charger's entities. Turn the other controller off for the charger SpotNav controls. The warning is for the charger when the controller's setting names it, and for the installation when the controller cannot name one.

- EV Smart Charging (`ev_smart_charging`)
- EVSE Load Balancer (`evse_load_balancer`)
- PeaqEV (`peaqev`)

Tibber's smart charging is not detected, because Home Assistant cannot see it. The core Tibber integration only reads a linked charger or vehicle (sensors, no switch, number or service that charges; its Data API scopes are read-only), so the smart charging that Tibber runs for a charger linked in the Tibber app happens in Tibber's cloud. If the charger is linked to Tibber (or another app) for smart charging, turn that off in the app, or SpotNav and the app will fight. The Easee setup step says so. Sources: [Tibber in Home Assistant](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tibber) and the integration's source, `homeassistant/components/tibber` (Home Assistant 2026.9.2).

### Not supported

SpotNav recognises these chargers but cannot drive them; the flow stops with a message.

- Pod Point (`pod_point`): Its switch replaces the stored weekly schedule with one-second windows and is unavailable in manual mode, and the integration no longer works with the new Pod Home app
- Andersen (`andersen_ev`): Lock only
- CTEK Nanogrid Air (`ctek_nanogrid_air`)
- Elli (`elli_charger_ha`)
- Blue Current (`blue_current`): Stop only

### Not a charger

These integrations are recognised as not being EV chargers, so their devices are not offered when you choose the charger's device.

- Webasto ThermoConnect (`webastoconnect`)
- GARO G-CTRL (`webel_gctrl`)
- JuiceNet (`juicenet`)
- Smappee (`smappee`)

### A dumb charger behind a smart plug

A charger with no integration of its own, such as a granny charger or a simple wallbox, can be switched by a smart plug that reports power. Add it with **Manual**: the plug's switch is the **Charge control** and the plug's power sensor (device class power, W or kW) is the **Power sensor (smart plug)**. Both can be changed later in the card's charger settings.

- SpotNav integrates the power into an energy counter of its own (the "Energy from power" sensor, trapezoid between readings). A gap longer than the maximum measurement age is not integrated, and the counter is kept across restarts. It stands in for the energy register unless you choose one.
- With no status sensor, SpotNav reads "the car is finished or not drawing" from the power: below 100 W for five minutes during a planned charge, the card says the charger draws almost no power. The limit can be changed under the integration's **Configure** (*Not drawing below (W)*).
- The plug must be rated for the charger's continuous current (a charger at 16 A needs a plug that carries 16 A for hours, which many cheap plugs do not), and the charger must start charging again by itself when power returns. SpotNav can switch the plug but cannot tell the charger to start.
- There is no current control: the charger charges at its own current and SpotNav only switches it. SpotNav learns that current from the plug's power, and load balancing pauses and resumes the charge whole (see [chargers that can only be switched on and off](site-and-load-balancing.md#chargers-that-can-only-be-switched-on-and-off)).

## Supported grid meters

When you add a site, SpotNav scans the entity registry for these meters, including entities their integration ships disabled, and offers what it found. Nothing is applied until you confirm, and only entities the integration disabled are ever enabled. A meter that is not listed is still found when its entities carry a per-phase current or power and voltage, or you can pick the entities yourself.

Measurement is either direct (a current per phase) or derived (power and voltage per phase). Derived current is exact when the meter also reports its own current, apparent power or reactive power, and estimated from power with a power factor of 0.9 otherwise.

Solar and hybrid need the grid's signed power. A derived site has it per phase; a direct site has it only with the meter's total grid power, which the rows below mark where SpotNav detects it. Without it, pick the meter's total power sensor yourself in the site editor.

## Supported vehicles

SpotNav needs no vehicle integration to charge. A vehicle adds the target state of charge, the charge-level estimate and the charge-limit display. Any integration works when one of its devices has a battery percentage sensor and a distance (range) sensor: SpotNav detects the vehicle from those shapes, not from the brand. A Subaru e-Outback, for example, is detected through the Toyota integration (`pytoyoda`, Home Assistant domain `toyota`) from its battery level sensor and range sensor, although the list below has no Subaru-specific entry for it.

The integrations below are the ones the detection was checked against, from each integration's recorded entity shapes. A vehicle that reports several battery readings is ranked by what the integration calls them, and when that does not leave exactly one, Home Assistant shows a repair asking which reading is the state of charge.

### Known pitfalls

- **Health is not charge.** State-of-health, target, limit, minimum, arrival and predicted readings are never taken as the state of charge.
- **The 12 V battery.** Many integrations give the car's 12 V battery the battery device class. A device with only that sensor is not a vehicle.
- **Sleeping cars.** Cloud readings can be an hour old in the middle of a charge. SpotNav estimates the level forward from the charger's energy meter and marks it as estimated. The app's refresh, like SpotNav's own re-reads, only asks Home Assistant to re-read the vehicle's entities; SpotNav never calls an integration's own force-update. Most integrations answer that from their cloud's copy, but Kia Uvo (`kia_uvo`) asks the car itself when its last report is older than the integration's force-refresh interval (in the Australian region at every update), which can wake the car.
- **No range sensor, no vehicle.** A device without a distance-class range sensor, or with no device classes at all, is not detected. Nor is an integration that registers no device: Nissan Leaf (`nissan_leaf`) has no device and no device class on its ranges, and Volkswagen GoConnect (`volkswagen_goconnect`) none on its charge level or range.
- **A charge limit that is writable only in one mode.** The unofficial Polestar integration (`polestar`) accepts its charge target only while its own charging mode is custom. In daily or long-trip mode SpotNav's write fails and is reported as a failed charge limit.
- **The car's own solar charging.** Teslemetry's (`teslemetry`) charge on solar and its lower limit drive Tesla's own solar charging. Turn it off for a car SpotNav charges: two controllers on one charge fight each other, as with a charger's built-in PV mode.
- Shapes the detection was checked to leave alone:
  - `cupra_we_connect`: Range sensor without a distance class is a miss.
  - `kia_uvo HEV`: The 12 V battery keeps the battery class and is not an EV.
  - `kia_uvo before the API answered`: Only the 12 V sensor and a range.
  - `toyota_na`: No device classes at all is a miss.

## Supported solar forecast

The Hybrid strategy holds back grid energy when a solar forecast promises sun. It reads the forecast through the Energy dashboard's solar forecast contract, so any integration that feeds the Energy dashboard's solar forecast can be chosen on the site. SpotNav only reads the estimate an integration already has and never asks it to fetch. Forecasts in 15, 30 or 60 minute slots are summed per hour. Without a source, Hybrid plans exactly like Cheapest.

| Source | What it is | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Forecast.Solar (`forecast_solar`) | Chosen on the site; read through the Energy dashboard. | Detected from the integration's source |
| Solcast Solar (`solcast_solar`) | Chosen on the site; read through the Energy dashboard. | Tested: charging verified (Solcast) |
| Open-Meteo Solar Forecast (`open_meteo_solar_forecast`) | Chosen on the site; read through the Energy dashboard. | Detected from the integration's source |
| [SpotNav's own solar forecast](forecasts.md#spotnavs-own-solar-forecast-background-only) | Built in, no integration to add: an irradiance forecast from [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/) (weather data by Open-Meteo.com, CC BY 4.0), fetched by your own Home Assistant, and your own measured solar production. | Runs in the background only: logged and scored each night beside the source you chose, and not yet used by Hybrid or any other plan |

Whichever source you choose, Solcast included, SpotNav learns a correction for it from your own production (a factor for clear hours and one for cloudy hours). The battery plan reads the corrected forecast once the correction has learnt; Hybrid keeps reading the forecast as the source gives it. See [the solar forecast correction](forecasts.md#the-solar-forecast-correction).

## Supported price areas

Your Home Assistant fetches the prices itself, from a source you add once ([Prices](prices.md#where-prices-come-from)):

| Areas | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Germany/Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, Austria, Poland, Romania, Bulgaria | Home Assistant's built-in Nord Pool integration (or your own ENTSO-E key) |
| Switzerland, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Croatia, Greece, Italy (all zones), Spain (day-ahead), Portugal | Your own free ENTSO-E key (the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform) |
| Spain – PVPC (regulated) | Home Assistant's built-in PVPC integration (Red Eléctrica) |
| Great Britain – Octopus Agile, 14 regions | The Octopus Energy integration (HACS), your Agile meter |
| Netherlands – Zonneplan | The Zonneplan integration (HACS), Zonneplan's dynamic tariff |

The card's area picker lists every area and names, in the price settings, where its prices come from or what to add. The SpotNav relay no longer delivers prices (since SpotNav 2.0).

### Great Britain (Octopus Agile)

- **For Agile customers.** The prices are Octopus Energy's Agile import unit rates, one per region (`GB-A` to `GB-P`, the GSP groups), in half-hours that SpotNav plans on quarter-hours. On any other tariff they are not your prices.
- **All-in.** The Agile unit rate already contains VAT, levies and network charges, so VAT, energy tax and grid transfer are locked as *Included in the price* and nothing is added. The daily standing charge is not part of a plan or a session's cost.
- **Your region.** The picker groups the regions under Great Britain ("GB C – London"). *Find my region* takes a postcode: Home Assistant asks Octopus Energy's public lookup directly, and the postcode is not sent anywhere else, stored or logged. A new charger in Great Britain starts with no area until you choose one.
- **Your rates.** They are read from your own meter through the [Octopus Energy](https://github.com/BottlecapDave/HomeAssistant-OctopusEnergy) integration, installed through HACS. Without an Agile meter there are no prices.
- **When.** Agile is published around 16:00 UK time for 23:00 to 23:00, so tomorrow's last hour (23:00 to midnight) arrives with the next day's publication. Amounts are in pounds and pence and distances in miles.
- **Not with Intelligent Octopus Go.** Octopus does not allow a third party to control the charging of a car on Intelligent Octopus Go: its customers must opt out of other apps' smart charging. Do not use SpotNav to control charging on that tariff. Source: [Octopus Energy](https://octopus.energy/help-and-faqs/articles/why-can-t-i-have-both-intelligent-octopus-go-and-a-third-party-controlling-my-charging-/).

Prices: Octopus Energy (Agile). SpotNav is not affiliated with Octopus Energy.

### Netherlands (Zonneplan)

- **For Zonneplan customers.** *Netherlands – Zonneplan* (`NL-ZONNEPLAN`) is Zonneplan's dynamic tariff per kWh, in quarter-hours. The area *Netherlands* (`NL`) stays the day-ahead spot price with your own fees; the two never share days or a price history.
- **All-in.** The tariff already contains Zonneplan's purchase fee, the energy tax and VAT, so VAT and energy tax are locked as *Included in the price* and nothing is added. Grid transfer stays a normal setting, off by default: Dutch network costs are per connection, not per kWh.
- **Your prices.** They are read from the [Zonneplan](https://github.com/fsaris/home-assistant-zonneplan-one) integration, installed through HACS (its sensor *Current quarter hourly electricity tariff* must be on). SpotNav does not contact Zonneplan itself. While that integration is loaded and the area *Netherlands* has prices of its own, it shows a hint to choose *Netherlands – Zonneplan*. When it is down there is no fallback to the spot price: the days already held keep planning, and tomorrow waits.
- **When.** Tomorrow's tariff appears in the afternoon, after the day-ahead auction. If the integration's forecast right after Zonneplan is added starts at the current quarter-hour rather than at midnight, that first day is not used (SpotNav never fills in prices it does not have): tomorrow's tariff is fetched in the afternoon, and charging is planned from midnight, when it becomes today's.

Prices: Zonneplan. SpotNav is not affiliated with Zonneplan.
